summary: Parkevtate Vosianc's September 22 video compares two beaten-down athletic apparel stocks trading near 52-week lows to pick the better buying opportunity. Nike is the bigger company ($46B trailing sales vs Lululemon's $11B), but Lululemon was growing faster before both hit headwinds. Both face muted sales ahead with downgraded guidance and macro pressures (tariffs, declining disposable income). Lululemon wins on quality metrics: operating margin of 18% vs Nike's 8.8% (though Nike's figure was flattered by a ~$1B tariff refund after the Supreme Court ruled some tariffs illegal; organically Nike is using more promotions to clear excess inventory, and its margins are falling), and ROIC of 21.4% vs Nike's 12.4%. On valuation, Nike trades at a forward P/E of 15.7 vs Lululemon's 11.4 — Nike at a premium he isn't sure it deserves, given Nike's 'extensive troubles': rising competition, excess inventory, and the hard work of rebuilding wholesaler relationships damaged by the prior CEO's direct-to-consumer push. His DCF gives Nike a $31 fair value vs $36 market price (slightly overvalued on DCF, undervalued on P/E — slightly undervalued overall), while Lululemon is undervalued on both metrics with a $126 fair value vs a $100 market price. Fair disclosure: he owns Lululemon, bought a year ago, and is down significantly. Both are ranked buying opportunities, but if forced to pick one he chooses Lululemon for the better valuation, margins and lighter turnaround burden. Calls per supplied list: NKE BUY @ $36; LULU BUY @ $100.
